reason: Cold outer orbits should help preserve ice, directly advancing the snow-line goal.
expectation: I expect the icy dust to remain frozen or accumulate in the outer disk, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust could advance the inner-disk story, but I chose the clearer ice-storage route first.

effect: The outer-disk ice store completes that goal, so I’ll turn to the inner disk.
reaction: The distinction between surviving inherited ice and refrozen vapor was useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may establish how the young Sun affects the disk.
expectation: I expect the Sun to heat the disk and reveal a path toward the rocky inner mixture, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The Sun and disk established a hot inner region, pointing toward the rocky-mixture goal.
reaction: The role of both sunlight and accretion in heating was useful context.
reason: This is the only offered combination and continues the inner-disk route.
expectation: I expect it to develop the hot inner-disk material, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The hottest inner-disk grains evaporated, leaving vapor that can be reprocessed.
reaction: It was useful to see that inherited grains need not survive intact.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should allow the vapor to cool toward rocky material.
expectation: I expect escaping radiation to cool the vapor, possibly allowing solids to condense; the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Cooling produced refractory grains, which can now be combined with rock-forming dust.
reaction: The contrast between high-temperature mineral condensation and ice preservation is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly connects the new grains to the rocky-mixture goal.
expectation: I expect a rocky mixture containing refractory grains, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The grains formed a loose rocky aggregate, which can now undergo intense heating.
reaction: The different possible grain histories were interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and continues the rocky-mixture route.
expectation: I expect the brief heating to alter or partly melt the aggregate, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Brief heating produced molten droplets, which can now cool.
reaction: Leaving the disputed heating mechanism open is a useful qualification.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should cool the droplets.
expectation: I expect the droplets to solidify as radiation carries away heat, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The droplets cooled into chondrules, which can now join metal grains.
reaction: Their textures preserving evidence of rapid heating and cooling are interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the rocky-mixture goal.
expectation: I expect a mixture of chondrules and metal grains, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The chondrules and metal formed a rocky-body ingredient mixture, completing the remaining goal without yet forming a planet.
reaction: The distinction between assembling ingredients and forming a planet was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the molten droplets into chondrules was most worthwhile: their textures preserve evidence of rapid heating and cooling.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of single offered combinations became somewhat repetitive, even though the cooling steps made physical sense.

surprise.text: I was surprised that inherited ice can survive in the outer disk rather than every grain melting and refreezing.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the cause of the brief intense heating was left open as a disputed mechanism.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the rocky and icy ingredients become larger bodies, especially after the chapter distinguished raw materials from planets.
